records.name: Rivers
records.summary:
No regional protective statute, recorded incident series or documented enforcement divergence from the national framework has been documented for this state. The national framework applies in full: a 2014 statute punishes same-sex unions with up to 14 years' imprisonment and — as reported in August 2026 summarising a foreign government's travel advisory — also reaches assisting, attending or promoting same-sex ceremonies and LGBT+ organisations; religious criminal law in some northern states can carry the death penalty for same-sex conduct. The same advisory warns LGBT+ travellers to this country of arrest, violence, blackmail and intimidation.

The recorded violence pattern is national and recent: a 33-year-old transgender media personality and sex worker was beaten to death in the federal capital in August 2024, having reported a stabbing a year earlier and said she feared for her life; authorities ordered a discreet investigation. Mass arrests and detention of LGBT+ people remain common, concentrated in some northern states. The absence of state-specific records here reflects thin documentation rather than demonstrated safety.

records.name: Kwara
records.summary:
Kwara lies within Nigeria's uniform criminalisation framework: the same-sex marriage prohibition law carries up to 14 years' imprisonment for same-sex conduct and also reaches people who help arrange or attend same-sex weddings. An allied government's August 2026 travel advice warns LGBT+ travellers nationwide to Nigeria of arrest, violence, attacks, blackmail and intimidation.

Trans-specific risk is documented nationally: a national broadcaster reported mass arrests and detention of LGBTQ+ people as common, especially in northern states, and the 2024 beating-death of a prominent transgender creator in the capital — after an earlier stabbing she had said left her fearing for her life — shows lethal violence against visibly trans people, with an investigation announced but no accountability recorded in the sources.

No state-specific sources for Kwara survived audit, so no local divergence is claimed in either direction; as a north-central state it sits close to, though sources do not name it among, the northern states where Sharia criminal provisions can compound the national penalties.
